title: They came with stones in their hands… but sin in their hearts.
paragraphs: They came with stones in their hands… but sin in their hearts.
Because the loudest accusers are not always the cleanest souls.

Scriptures memorized.
Voices firm.
Convictions sharp like the rocks they were ready to throw.
Because if we’re honest—this story isn’t just about them.

That quiet thought you justify.
That secret habit you hide.
That moment you judged someone… while excusing yourself.
We don’t always carry stones in our hands.
Sometimes we carry them in our hearts.
Let me open the tension wider.

You can sit in church every Sunday…
Lift your hands in worship…
Post Bible verses online…
And still be silently building a courtroom in your mind.

Where you are the judge.
They are the accused.
And mercy… is nowhere to be found.
In John 8:7, the moment breaks open:
“Let any one of you who is without sin be the first to throw a stone.”
Just truth… sharp enough to cut through pride.

The same hands that were ready to throw…
Start to tremble.
Because conviction has a way of exposing what performance tries to hide.
“For all have sinned and fall short of the glory of God.”

The religious.
The rebellious.
The quiet.
The loud.
Every single one of us has missed the mark.
Here’s the part that will humble you if you let it:
The distance between you and the person you judge…
Some scholars interpret the scene in John 8 as Jesus writing the hidden sins of the accusers on the ground.
We’re not told exactly what He wrote.
Because when light hits the truth…
Let me say this with love, but with fire:

Pride loves to expose others.
Grace starts by exposing you.
Because this is where religion ends… and the Gospel begins.
“Woman, where are they? Has no one condemned you?” (John 8:10)
Then He speaks words that still shake eternity:
“Neither do I condemn you… go, and sin no more.” (John 8:11)
But He didn’t crush her with it either.
But instead of throwing the stone at us…
Jesus took the weight of it on Himself.
“God made Him who had no sin to be sin for us, so that in Him we might become the righteousness of God.”
The only One who had the right to judge you…
Chose to be judged for you.
So now the question is no longer:
Because grace is not permission to stay the same.
You can’t keep holding stones… and follow Jesus at the same time.
You realize you’ve been the one judging.
Quick to speak. Slow to love.
You’ve been the one crushed by shame.
Carrying guilt like a weight on your chest.
And His invitation is the same.
“If we confess our sins, He is faithful and just and will forgive us our sins and purify us from all unrighteousness.”

That means no matter how hidden…
No matter how repeated…
No matter how heavy…
And every time you ignore it… your heart hardens a little more.
Where have you been holding stones?
Where have you been hiding sin?
Jesus is not waiting to destroy you.
